title: Attention Sinks and Outliers in Attention Residuals
claim: The standard approach lets normalization force mass onto outlier tokens and branches, causing sinks; ours adds explicit null routes that absorb it.
layout: 3 panels, left-to-right; baseline left, ours center, coupling detail right
description: The figure is split by a vertical dashed line into the baseline on the left and the proposed method on the right. The left panel, titled 'Standard AttnResidual', shows two blue boxes, one for token-level softmax and one for depth-level softmax. Each contains a bar chart with a red outlier bar and the constraint that probabilities sum to 1. Arrows feed these into circled-plus residual adds, and a red starburst reads 'Attention Sinks, Activation Outliers, Depth Collapse!'. The center panel, 'OASIS (Ours)', is a green dashed box with token-level and depth-level Softmax1 bar charts. Each has a hatched orange null bar in place of the red outlier. Formulas sit above the charts, and the output is a weighted residual update. The right panel is a yellow box with three steps for token-to-depth null coupling: a head-level null statistic, mean centering, and score injection into the depth logits. A dashed yellow arrow links the token null state to this box.
caption: Comparison of standard AttnResidual and OASIS. OASIS adds null-aware token- and depth-level routing with token-to-depth null coupling, enabling explicit no-op allocation and reducing no-op outlier pressure, sink accumulation, and depth-collapse pressure.
abstract: We propose OASIS, an outlier- and sink-aware method that stabilizes dual-normalized attention-residual architectures through explicit null routing and token-to-depth null coupling. AttnResidual introduces an additional depth-wise normalization channel that improves inter-layer routing flexibility but can also amplify attention sinks, activation outliers, and low-bit quantization error. OASIS builds on explicit Softmax1-based null routes at both the token and depth levels and uses token-level null evidence to downweight depth branches exhibiting stronger null behavior. Theoretically, we characterize a conditional mechanism for sink-like attention concentration under dual normalization, offering insight into the low-bit sensitivity observed in AttnResidual. Experimentally, we compare OASIS against five baselines on three language-model backbones and multiple language-modeling, reasoning, and long-context benchmarks and observe consistent improvements in both attention sink mitigation and post-quantization performance. Notably, relative to Vanilla AttnResidual, OASIS reduces maximum infinity norm by 81.75% and average kurtosis by 95.90%, lowers W8A8 perplexity by 82.00%, and improves W4A4 GSM8K Pass@1 by 42.11% on average across LLaMA-3.2-1B, Qwen3-0.6B, and Phi-4. Code is available at: https://github.com/robinzixuan/OASIS.
